claim: For the Memarzadeh--Mancini channel restricted to the qutrit Fock space \(\operatorname{span}\{|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|2\rangle\}\), impose the mean-energy constraint \(N=3/2\) and take pure dephasing \(\epsilon=1\). For every \(0<t\le \log(4/3)\), the admissible adjacent-level state \(|\chi\rangle=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2\) has strictly smaller output von Neumann entropy than every candidate allowed by Conjecture 1 of Memarzadeh and Mancini (2016): the unique admissible binomial state, with \(M=2\) and \(\mu=3/4\), and every phase-equivalent endpoint state \(|\kappa_\alpha\rangle=\tfrac12|0\rangle+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}e^{2i\alpha}|2\rangle\). Hence Conjecture 1 is false already in dimension three, and in fact fails on the whole nontrivial interval \(0<t\le\log(4/3)\).

correctness.rationale: At pure dephasing the source channel acts entrywise as exp(-(m-n)^2 t). The witness spectrum is exactly {0,(1-q)/2,(1+q)/2}. For each conjectured candidate, the output purity is computed exactly. Both purities lie below the sharp three-eigenvalue lower bound forced by any largest eigenvalue at least (1+q)/2 throughout q in [3/4,1). This forces a strictly smaller largest eigenvalue and hence strictly larger von Neumann entropy than the witness. The inequalities are symbolic and valid on the full interval; finite sampling is not used.

value.rationale: The claim gives an exact continuum of low-dimensional counterexamples to a published minimum-output-entropy conjecture that was supported by a 100,000-state random search. The witness exposes a substantive structural omission in the proposed ansatz: at energies above one quantum, an adjacent pair of excited Fock levels can preserve dephasing coherence better than either the binomial family or the farthest-separated endpoint pair. This directly changes the finite-dimensional optimization problem rather than merely sharpening a decimal value.
